findings.suggested_form: if sender.push(ev).is_err() { return ScheduleResult::Err { error: "audio event queue full — schedule dropped".to_owned() }; } ScheduleResult::Ok { accepted }
findings.rationale: The prior code and docs (audio.md:97-98 "A full event queue also returns ScheduleResult::Err") require queue-full to be observable. Dropping the Result with `let _ =` and unconditionally returning Ok violates that contract: a caller with a valid batch receives `accepted == mail.events.len()` while zero events were enqueued, causing silent loss of the entire atomic batch. Restoring the `is_err()` branch makes failure observable and matches the pre-change behavior.

Function contracts to return Result<T, FrameError> and has From<io::Error> for FrameError::Io; the second body read already uses ?. Unwrap turns any runtime I/O failure on the 4-byte prefix (EOF, UnexpectedEof, broken pipe) into a panic/unwind instead of a recoverable Err, violating the Result contract and crashing library callers. Propagating with ? restores parity with the body read and with the pre-change code.

Shelf packer invariant is that shelf_height tracks the padded extent (height+GLYPH_PADDING) so next shelf's y includes the 1px gutter. Using unpadded height makes shelf_y advance short by 1px per shelf, packing the next row into the previous row's gutter and violating the non-overlap / bilinear-bleed isolation the constant documents. Restoring padded_height preserves the documented gutter and keeps the full-check (shelf_y + padded_height) consistent with the advance.

findings.current_form: if let TraceEvent::Sent { recipient, .. } = entry.event { if self.visited.contains(&recipient) { continue; } self.frontier.push_back(recipient); } self.collected.push(entry);
findings.suggested_form: if let TraceEvent::Sent { recipient, .. } = entry.event && !self.visited.contains(&recipient) { self.frontier.push_back(recipient); } self.collected.push(entry); // always collect, dedup only controls frontier push
findings.rationale: The `continue` couples mailbox-dedup to event-collection: when `recipient` was already visited, the entire `TraceRingEntry` (the Sent that defines that child mail_id) is skipped and never reaches `collected`/`fold_nodes`. The contract is to dedup frontier visits but collect every in-root Sent regardless of visit order — a `Sent`'s authority is its `mail_id`, not its `recipient`. Restoring the original guard so `collected.push` is unconditional preserves all nodes and makes BFS order irrelevant, which is strictly more correct and no less clear.

findings.current_form: Vec::with_capacity(len.min(cur.bytes.len())) // clamps Vec pre-allocation to total input length
findings.suggested_form: Vec::with_capacity(len.min(cur.remaining())) // clamp to bytes not yet consumed
findings.rationale: The changed line contradicts its own comment ('clamp the pre-allocation against the bytes that remain') and the identical Map arm at ~378 which correctly uses cur.remaining(). Using cur.bytes.len() (total) instead of cur.remaining() (= len-pos) doubles-to-many-times the allowed capacity for any Vec decoded after pos>0 (e.g., second field of a struct or inner Vec after a large prior field). A crafted u32 len can then drive Vec::with_capacity up to total input size even when only a few bytes remain, reopening the OOM/decompression-bomb the clamp was meant to bound; the per-value budget only checks inside the loop, after the allocation.

findings.current_form: self.dirty = true; set before rect_in_bounds / pixels.len() validation, so `if !rect_in_bounds || pixels.len() != rect_bytes { return false; }` returns false with dirty already flipped (line 41 before line 44)
findings.suggested_form: validate first and return false without mutating state; set self.dirty = true only on the success path (after the bounds/length check, before or after the row copy, as in the pre-change version)
findings.rationale: Doc contract and struct invariant require `false` means "without touching staged pixels" and `dirty` means "staging has diverged from GPU and needs re-upload" (see StagedTexture docs line 18-20 and ensure_realized line 63-81). Dirty-on-failure breaks both: a clean texture with a malformed update (e.g., width=2 height=2 dirty=false; apply_subrect(1,0,2,1,&[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]) out-of-bounds, or apply_subrect(0,0,1,1,&[1,2,3]) length mismatch) now returns false but leaves dirty=true, causing the next ensure_realized to spuriously re-upload unchanged pixels and violating the caller expectation in render/runtime/mod.rs:427 that a dropped update leaves staging untouched.

Current else-branch computes alpha*prev + (1-alpha)*sample instead of (1-alpha)*prev + alpha*sample. For prev=100ms, sample=10ms, alpha=0.2 correct EWMA is 82ms (20% toward sample) but current gives 28ms (80% toward sample), violating the documented 200-permille smoothing invariant and the comment next = prev ± alpha*|delta|. The fix restores symmetric 20% weighting and makes up/down moves consistent; existing test only covers upward samples so the inversion is not caught.

findings.suggested_form: let pan_norm = (if pan < 0 { f32::from(pan) / 128.0 } else { f32::from(pan) / 127.0 }).clamp(-1.0, 1.0); // or revert to /127.0 clamped
findings.rationale: Doc contract on lines 581-582 promises -128 hard-left and 127 hard-right (gain_l=0,gain_r=1). With /128.0, pan=127 yields 127/128=0.9921875 -> theta~(0.992+1)*pi/4 < pi/2 so [cos,sin]~[0.012,0.9999], leaking ~1.2% into left vs invariant silent. Old /127.0 clamped gave both hards exact (-128 clamped, 127 exact). Asymmetric i8 needs asymmetric divisor to hit both edges; single /128.0 breaks the hard-right invariant while fixing duplicate mapping of -128/-127.

findings.current_form: let bytes = fs::read(path).await.map_err(...)?; serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(...)?  // no size check before allocation/parse
findings.suggested_form: let bytes = fs::read(path).await.map_err(...)?; if bytes.len() > max_frame_size() { return Err(McpError::invalid_params(format!("{context}: config_path {path:?} is {} bytes, over the {}-byte RPC frame cap", bytes.len(), max_frame_size()), None)); } serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(...)? // or metadata/limited-reader pre-check to avoid allocating over cap
findings.rationale: config_path is user-supplied (tool args) and fs::read allocates the whole file unbounded. Inline `config` is already bounded by the inbound RPC frame, and Bytes embeds via `$file` are bounded by max_frame_size() inside resolve_bytes_params, but the outer config_path read has no budget cap. Concrete path: LoadComponent with config_path=/tmp/huge.json (e.g., 1+ GiB of JSON) causes the MCP process to allocate and parse gigabytes before any later frame-size error, OOM/abort instead of returning a bounded McpError::invalid_params. Checking bytes.len() against max_frame_size() (the same cap used for resolve_bytes_params) makes the failure bounded and consistent with the existing embed guard.

findings.current_form: let Some((ptr,len)) = self.write_guest(blob) else { return; }; let _ = self.store.set_fuel(self.fuel_per_call); let _ = load.call(&mut self.store,(ptr,len));
findings.suggested_form: if self.store.set_fuel(self.fuel_per_call).is_err() { tracing::warn!(target: "aether_behavior","state_load fuel budget could not be set; dropping migration blob (fail-open)"); return; } let Some((ptr,len)) = self.write_guest(blob) else { return; }; if let Err(e) = load.call(&mut self.store,(ptr,len)) { tracing::warn!(target: "aether_behavior", error=%e, "state_load trapped; leaving fresh script untouched (fail-open)"); }
findings.rationale: write_guest calls the guest alloc export which consumes fuel, so the budget must be installed before the allocation as filter_inner and save_state do. With the current order a fresh Store (initial fuel 0 when consume_fuel is true) traps on alloc, write_guest returns None and the valid prior blob is silently dropped, violating the documented swap-carry invariant that old state_save is offered to the new state_load. Checking set_fuel first makes the install explicit, fail-open with a diagnostic like save_state, and keeps allocation+call under the same budget.

lintCandidates.note: let _ = on Result (set_fuel, TypedFunc::call) triggers clippy::let_underscore_must_use / must_use - mechanically detectable, but whether discarding is a defect requires the fail-open contract reasoning above, so the ordering/budget bug is a finding not just a lint.

findings.suggested_form: remove the test; if wire-identity stability must be guarded, replace with a computed tripwire on what consumers actually route on: assert_eq!(Mat4Apply::ID, KindId(0x…)) with tripwire comment
findings.rationale: Exercised logic: none owned by this crate. Mat4Apply::NAME is the literal from #[kind(name = "aether.math.mat4_apply")] at crates/aether-kinds/src/math.rs:26 emitted by #[derive(Kind)] owned by aether-data. The assertion restates that declaration (derived-constant mirror per docs/guide/testing.md: assert_eq!(NoteOn::NAME, "...")). It cannot fail independently — a rename edits the attribute and the literal in the same commit, and every real consumer routes on Mat4Apply::NAME/ID so tracks the rename for free. Pinned value is not COMPUTED (not a hash/bytes/KindId), so it is not the tripwire carve-out which requires a computed value that drifts when producing logic changes. Removing is at least as safe/correct: eliminates compile/run cost and false coverage without losing signal; a KindId tripwire would be strictly stronger if stability is required.

findings.current_form: fn font_metrics_survives_a_wire_roundtrip() — symmetric aether_data::wire::to_vec -> from_bytes roundtrip over FontMetrics/GlyphAdvance asserting each decoded field == original
findings.suggested_form: Remove. If wire stability of the metrics grab must be pinned, add a computed-value tripwire in the owning crate (aether-data) pinning golden bytes / hash, not a symmetric roundtrip in aether-kinds.
findings.rationale: FontMetrics and GlyphAdvance are plain #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Schema, PartialEq)] with plain f32/Vec fields (lib.rs:1060,1078) and no hand-written ser/de, clamp, or normalization. aether_data::wire::to_vec/from_bytes is owned and tested in aether-data (wire/mod.rs:99,106). The test exercises no logic owned by aether-kinds — the only owned logic in this file is scale_units/CachedFontMetrics — and is symmetric: a shape change regenerates both encode and decode in lockstep so decoded==original still passes. It cannot catch the claimed 'wire shape break'; a true tripwire would pin computed golden bytes. Removing it is clearer/safer because it stops paying compile/run/reviewer cost for false coverage while keeping the two load-bearing tests that exercise owned scaling and caret arithmetic.
